hypothesis: Different buyer than Shopify-natives. FBA inbound-shipment planning is the killer feature. Higher SKU count, less branded community, more 'operator' mindset. Many will be supplements/cosmetics/pet/homewares.

market_sizing.target_buyer: Private-label brand owner or operations lead at a 2-15 person Amazon-FBA business. Often a solo or duo founder who built the brand on Amazon first and may have added Shopify/Woo as secondary channels. Buyer is metric-driven, FBA-fee-conscious, and treats inbound-shipment planning as the most painful workflow.
market_sizing.business_count_au: ~1,500-3,000 AU Amazon-FBA private-label sellers (Amazon AU launched 2017, base growing; AU FBA is smaller than US/UK FBA but maturing). Estimated 2,500 active third-party AU sellers with manufacturing/private-label shape vs reseller/dropship shape [uncertain].
market_sizing.business_count_secondary: US ~120,000-180,000 (largest by orders of magnitude); UK ~25,000-40,000; CA ~15,000-25,000; NZ negligible (no Amazon NZ marketplace). US is the realistic secondary target post-launch; AU is small but high-quality cohort. [uncertain].
market_sizing.typical_size: 2-15 FTE (skews smaller than Shopify Plus due to FBA outsourcing fulfilment), AU$500K-AU$10M revenue. Higher revenue-per-FTE than Shopify-native segments because FBA replaces warehouse/3PL/fulfilment staff.
market_sizing.annual_revenue_band_aud: $1M-$5M most common; $500K-$1M tail; $5M-$10M head. Growth ($249) and Pro ($499) candidates predominantly.
market_sizing.growth_trend: Amazon AU base growing 15-25% YoY (Amazon Australia FY24 disclosures + Marketplace Pulse). US/UK FBA base relatively mature (~3-5% YoY new sellers, higher churn). AU is the fastest-growing FBA market in absolute terms but smallest base. Aggregate accessible-to-Manuva segment is growing steadily.
market_sizing.seasonality_intensity: 5 — Heaviest seasonality of any segment. Q4 (Prime Big Deal Days October + Black Friday + Christmas) drives 40-50% of annual volume. Inbound planning intensifies July-November. Q1 is restocking + post-Q4 audit. Two intense buying windows: pre-Q4 (July-September) and Q1 (Jan-March).

fit_and_timing.manuva_fit_score: 3 — Mid. Manuva's core (BOMs, inventory, POs, lot tracking) fits private-label makers cleanly, BUT FBA-specific workflows (inbound shipment plans, FNSKU/ASIN labelling, multi-FC inventory placement, removal orders, restock recommendations) are unique to Amazon and require dedicated connector depth beyond a basic order-sync. Fit-score is gated on FBA connector depth — basic order-sync = 2; full FBA inbound-planning workflow = 4.
fit_and_timing.addressable_window: after Amazon — fully gated on Amazon connector shipping. Pre-connector, Manuva cannot serve this segment meaningfully.
roadmap_dependency: Amazon connector (must-have, gating) — depth matters: order ingestion is necessary but inbound-shipment planning is what wins this segment
Amazon SP-API integration covering FBA inventory + inbound shipments + removal orders + multi-marketplace
Lot tracking (must-have for the ~50% supplements/cosmetics/food slice of FBA) — already shipped pre-launch
Xero/MYOB/QuickBooks integration (~70% — FBA settlement reports need accounting sync)
Multi-currency support (US/UK FBA sellers operating from AU need USD/GBP revenue capture)
FNSKU/ASIN management, expiry-date labelling for supplements, FBA fee calculator integration (nice-to-have)
fit_and_timing.typical_tier: Growth ($249) for ~50%; Pro ($499) for ~45% (multi-marketplace + accounting integration heavier users); Starter ($99) for ~5% (very early FBA sellers).
fit_and_timing.regulatory_burden: 3 — Higher than Shopify-native segments because FBA-supplements + FBA-cosmetics + FBA-food carry both AU compliance (TGA/AICIS/FSANZ) AND Amazon's own gating + GMP audit requirements. Lot tracking + expiry dates + COA storage are FBA operational requirements not just regulatory.
fit_and_timing.lot_batch_criticality: 4 — High. Amazon FBA requires lot codes + expiry dates labelled on inbound shipments for supplements, cosmetics, food. Manuva's pre-launch lot tracking is necessary; FBA-specific labelling workflow is desirable.
fit_and_timing.time_to_value_days: 12-25 days. Initial setup more involved than Shopify segments because of FBA's multi-marketplace + multi-fulfilment-channel complexity. First successful inbound shipment plan via Manuva = day 10-14.

economics.incumbent_pricing: Stack today: Amazon Seller Central Professional US$39.99/mo + FBA fees (variable, 15-30% of revenue), plus a heavily fragmented tooling ecosystem. Common FBA-specific tools: Helium 10 (US$99-349/mo), Jungle Scout (US$49-149/mo), SoStocked (US$77-419/mo — most direct competitor for inventory + inbound planning), Forecastly (acquired by SoStocked), RestockPro (US$99-299/mo), InventoryLab ($69/mo), Sellboard. Light MRP/manufacturing players: Katana (~10% of FBA users), Cin7/DEAR (~5%), MRPeasy (~5%), spreadsheets (~55%). The FBA-specific inventory-planning slot is owned by SoStocked / RestockPro / Helium 10 — none of which do BOMs or supplier management. Manuva's wedge: combine the FBA inbound layer with the BOM/supplier layer that FBA-natives currently lack.
economics.willingness_to_pay_aud: $249-499/mo is well within FBA-seller budget norms (they routinely pay US$300-600/mo across Helium 10 + SoStocked + accounting tools). WTP is high if the FBA-specific workflow value is real.
economics.expansion_revenue_potential: 4 — Strong. Multi-marketplace expansion (AU → US → UK → CA) drives natural Pro-tier upgrades. Capacity-planning + inbound-forecasting modules can be add-on revenue. NRR potential 115-130%.
economics.churn_risk: 4 — Higher than Shopify segments. Reasons: (a) FBA business mortality is high (Amazon policy changes, account suspensions, category bans wipe out brands), (b) FBA private-label is operator-mindset, prone to tool-stack churn / consolidation, (c) Amazon itself adds native features (e.g. Amazon's own restock-planning improvements) that can erode wedge. Mitigation: lock in annual via discount, build deep BOM/supplier moat that FBA-native tools can't match.
economics.cac_estimate_aud: Cash CAC: AU$200-500 (Amazon-seller-keyword search ads, podcast sponsorships, FBA-community memberships). Founder-time CAC: 15-25 hrs/close × AU$150 = AU$2,250-3,750. Blended notional CAC AU$2,500-4,200.
economics.cash_cac_affordability: 3 — Higher than defection segments. FBA keyword competition is heavy (Helium 10 et al outbid). Affordable for solo founder but requires ~AU$200-500/customer cash commitment.
economics.ltv_estimate_aud: $390 ARPU × 80% margin × ~24 months × 1.2 NRR ≈ AU$8,900 LTV.
economics.ltv_cac_ratio: ~2-4:1 blended; ~18-30:1 cash-only. Borderline on blended — needs disciplined positioning to clear 3:1.
economics.typical_seat_count: 2-6 users typical. FBA businesses run lean. Per-seat incumbents not the main competition.
economics.multi_channel_count: 2-4 typical (Amazon AU + Amazon US + Amazon UK + Shopify D2C; some + Walmart Marketplace, eBay, Faire). Highest multi-marketplace count of any segment.
economics.wholesale_b2b_mix: 10-30% wholesale (mostly Amazon Wholesale / Vendor Central conversions or B2B sub-channel; lower wholesale% than other manufacturer segments).

where_they_live.primary_channels: Reddit r/FulfillmentByAmazon (~200k), r/AmazonSeller (~150k), r/AmazonFBA (~100k); LinkedIn 'Amazon Sellers Australia' + 'FBA Sellers' groups; Facebook 'Amazon FBA High Rollers', 'Amazon Australia Sellers', 'AU Amazon Sellers' (~10-30k cross-membership); Slack/Discord communities: Helium 10 user groups, FBA Mastery, Million Dollar Sellers (private/paid, $5k-15k joining fee). Twitter/X FBA voices: Kevin King, Bradley Sutton, Greg Mercer. [uncertain] sizes.
where_they_live.directories_communities: Amazon Seller Forums (Amazon-owned, dense), Jungle Scout 'Top Brands' lists, Marketplace Pulse seller leaderboards, Helium 10 community, MyAmazonGuy network, Amazon Vendor Central directory, eCom Crew network, FBA Allstars network, Amazon-AU specific small directories. AU: Amazon Australia 'Aussie Pulse' seller updates.
where_they_live.industry_facebook_group_size: ~30-80k cross-membership across AU and global Amazon-FBA FB groups. Smaller AU-specific community than Shopify segments but engaged. [uncertain].
where_they_live.podcasts_voices: Serious Sellers Podcast (Helium 10), AM/PM Podcast (Manny Coats — Amazon-focused), My Wife Quit Her Job (Steve Chou), Amazing FBA podcast (UK), Marketplace Pulse podcast, eCom Crew podcast (Mike Jackness — AU+US slant). YouTube: Bradley Sutton, Kevin King, Travis Marziani.
where_they_live.events_trade_shows: Sell And Scale Summit (Helium 10's event, USA, ~2k attendees, USD 1-5k sponsorship); Prosper Show (Las Vegas, ~3k, USD 3-15k); Amazon Ads Unboxed (Amazon's own, USA/UK); Amazon Accelerate (Amazon's annual seller conference, free + sponsored slots); ASGTG (Amazon Sellers Gathering The Group, USA, ~500); AU-specific: Online Retailer Sydney has Amazon-AU presence, otherwise AU FBA-specific events are limited. Total Phase-3 event budget AU$15-40k if serious about US expansion; AU-only Phase-3 budget AU$5-10k.
where_they_live.search_keywords: 'Amazon FBA inventory software', 'FBA inbound shipment planning', 'SoStocked alternative', 'Helium 10 alternative inventory', 'Amazon FBA supplier management', 'FBA BOM software', 'Amazon FBA stock forecasting', 'Amazon Seller Central Xero integration', 'Amazon FBA Australia inventory', 'private label brand inventory software'.
where_they_live.community_density: 4 — High community density (FBA community is loud and active) but US-centric. AU-specific density is moderate.
where_they_live.founder_persona_homogeneity: 4 — Strong persona homogeneity: 28-45 year old operator-founder, often comes from a previous corporate / e-commerce background, metric-fluent, FBA-fee-obsessed. Cross-vertical (supplements / cosmetics / pet / homewares / kitchen / outdoors) but persona-uniform.

outreach_fit.cold_outbound_feasibility: 3 — FBA private-label sellers are notoriously hard to identify by name (brand listings on Amazon don't expose seller identity easily). Tools like Helium 10 Black Box, Jungle Scout, Marketplace Pulse can surface seller identities + revenue estimates for outbound. Cost moderate. Cold outbound is feasible but expensive; community/podcast inbound is more efficient.
outreach_fit.inbound_content_fit: 4 — Strong. FBA-keyword SEO is competitive (Helium 10 outranks most) but long-tail wins ('SoStocked alternative for AU FBA', 'Amazon FBA BOM software', 'FBA inbound planning with supplier management') are winnable. Podcast guest-spots on FBA shows are the highest-leverage inbound move.
outreach_fit.founder_market_fit_proxy: 3 — FBA community has 'are you really an FBA operator' credibility filter. Kasper as a SaaS founder without FBA operator history will face skepticism. Mitigation: partner with a known FBA voice or hire/contract an FBA-experienced advisor for credibility; or lead with the BOM/supplier-side wedge where Kasper's manufacturing background reads cleaner.
outreach_fit.case_study_acquisition_cost: Moderate-high — FBA sellers are reluctant to share supplier/cost detail publicly (competitive intelligence concerns). Case studies must anonymise specifics or focus on workflow benefits without revealing margins. 3-5 case studies in months 8-12 (post-Amazon-connector) realistic.
outreach_fit.case_study_appeal: 3 — FBA-brand case studies have community-internal appeal but lower cross-segment leverage than Shopify-Plus or candle/cosmetic Tier-A logos. Best framed as 'How [brand] saved 8 hours/week on inbound planning' rather than logo-led.

foot_in_door_fit.design_partner_appeal: 3 — Moderate. FBA operators will trade roadmap input for early access if the FBA-specific value is concrete (inbound shipment planning UI co-design). 1-2 strategic design partners feasible to shape the FBA connector experience.
foot_in_door_fit.paid_pilot_fit: 4 — Good. FBA buyers prefer commitment over free (they already pay $300-600/mo across stack tools — $249-499 is normal). 3-month paid pilot at Growth or Pro credited to annual conversion works well.
foot_in_door_fit.free_trial_extension_fit: 2 — Low. FBA community treats free trials as 'small-time' — paid commitment signals seriousness. Skip.
foot_in_door_fit.trial_to_paid_benchmark: Paid pilot 35-55% (slightly below ChartMogul 40-60% benchmark due to FBA-stack-tool churn norms); CC-required 14-day trial 22-30%; design-partner conversion 65-80%.
foot_in_door_fit.reference_value: 3 — Reference logos compound within FBA community but transfer poorly to other segments. Best paired with Manuva's BOM/supplier wedge messaging so FBA customers are framed as 'manufacturers who also sell on Amazon' rather than 'Amazon resellers'.
foot_in_door_fit.recommended_foot_in_door_motion: Phase-3-only (gated on Amazon connector). Two-track motion. Track A: Design partner — 2 strategic AU FBA brands (one supplements + one homewares/pet) at 6 months free Pro + roadmap input + co-marketed case study on launch. Track B: Paid pilot at Pro $499 × 3 months credited, sourced via (a) FBA-podcast guest spots on Serious Sellers Podcast + AM/PM Podcast + eCom Crew, (b) Helium 10 / Jungle Scout community presence, (c) AU-focused 'Amazon FBA inventory + BOM software' SEO content. Avoid head-on competition with SoStocked/RestockPro positioning; lead with 'manufacturing-grade BOMs + suppliers for FBA brands' angle. Layer accountant channel later as FBA accounting integration matures.
foot_in_door_fit.rollout_phase: Phase 3 (months 6-12, post-Amazon connector). Likely active months 7-12. US expansion Phase 4 (year 2+).

competitive_context.current_dominant_tool: Fragmented stack. FBA inventory: SoStocked (~15-20%), RestockPro (~10%), Helium 10 Inventory (~15-25% as part of bundle), Forecastly (acquired into SoStocked), spreadsheets (~50%). FBA suite tools: Helium 10 dominant (~50% of FBA sellers use it for keyword/PPC, ~20% use its inventory module). Manufacturing/BOM layer: Katana (~10%), Cin7/DEAR (~5%), MRPeasy (~5%), spreadsheets (~60%). No tool dominantly serves the 'manufacturer-who-sells-on-FBA' combined need.
competitive_context.switching_pain: 3 — Moderate. SoStocked / RestockPro have invested setup (SKU velocity history, lead times, custom rules). Helium 10 stack-stickiness is high. BOM tools are easier to switch from (most FBA sellers don't have real BOMs anyway).
competitive_context.competitor_gaps_for_this_segment: (1) SoStocked / RestockPro do inbound planning but no BOM, no supplier POs, no manufacturing workflow; (2) Helium 10 inventory is bundled but feature-shallow vs SoStocked; (3) Katana / MRPeasy don't have FBA depth; (4) Cin7/DEAR is heavy + expensive + weak FBA workflow; (5) No tool combines manufacturing-grade BOMs + supplier POs + FBA inbound planning + AU accounting; (6) Most FBA tools are USD-priced and US-feature-skewed — AU FBA sellers feel underserved. Clean wedge.
competitive_context.user_satisfaction_signals: FBA forums and r/FulfillmentByAmazon regularly debate 'best inventory tool for FBA private label' with no consensus. SoStocked has solid satisfaction but is critiqued for cost-scaling. Helium 10 satisfaction is high but inventory module is the weak link in their suite. AU FBA sellers specifically lament USD-only billing + no Xero/MYOB on most tools. Specific quotes [uncertain] without live re-query.
competitive_context.competitor_concentration: Fragmented — no tool above 25% share for the combined need. Concentrated for sub-needs (Helium 10 for keyword/PPC, SoStocked for inbound planning) but the combined 'BOM + supplier + FBA inbound + AU accounting' slot is unowned.
competitive_context.integration_dependency_list: Amazon SP-API (must-have, gating), Xero (~70%), MYOB (~10%), QuickBooks (~15-20%), Shopify (~40% who run secondary D2C), 3PL portals (eStore Logistics, Locad, Easyship), Walmart Marketplace API (~5% multi-marketplace), eBay (~10%), Helium 10 PPC data sync (nice-to-have integration target), Jungle Scout (similar).

partner_channels.xero_myob_partner_channel_fit: 3 — Moderate. Amazon FBA accounting is messy (settlement reports, FBA fees, multi-currency); some specialised AU accounting firms (e.g. Bean Ninjas, A2X-using firms) serve FBA sellers exclusively. ProAdvisor channel works but is concentrated in 5-10 FBA-specialist firms rather than the broad ProAdvisor pool. Partner with FBA-specialist accountants.
partner_channels.shopify_app_store_acquisition_fit: 2 — Modest. The 40% of FBA sellers running secondary Shopify D2C may discover Manuva there, but their primary motivation is FBA tooling not Shopify tooling.
partner_channels.shopify_plus_partner_potential: 2 — Modest. FBA-native brands rarely upgrade to Plus.
partner_channels.tpl_3pl_referral_potential: 3 — Moderate. AU 3PLs that handle FBA-prep (Locad, eStore Logistics) serve this segment and field stack conversations. Co-marketing fit.
partner_channels.industry_association_sponsorship: Sell And Scale Summit USD 1-5k; Prosper Show USD 3-15k; Amazon Accelerate (sponsored slots); FBA podcast sponsorships USD 500-3k/episode (Serious Sellers, AM/PM, eCom Crew); Helium 10 user-conference sponsorship USD 5-15k; Million Dollar Sellers private community presence (paid membership USD 5-15k). Total Phase-3 event/podcast budget AU$15-30k for serious US+AU presence; AU-only AU$5-10k.
partner_channels.partner_channel_potential: 3 — Decent on podcast + FBA-accountant channel; weak on agency channel (FBA agencies focus on PPC and listing optimisation, not inventory).

profitability_math.realistic_12mo_customer_count_solo: 4-8 paying customers in months 0-12, all back-loaded into months 7-12 due to Phase-3 gating on Amazon connector. Realistic landing: 6 customers by month 12, concentrated in months 8-12. Bandwidth: 20-30 hrs/customer onboarding (FBA setup complexity is real).
profitability_math.realistic_12mo_mrr_contribution_aud: AU$1,800-3,200 MRR by month 12 (6 customers × $390 blended ARPU = $2,340; bound by late-cohort timing — only ~5 months of acquisition possible in year 1).
profitability_math.path_to_first_3k_5k_mrr_aud: Minor contributor in year 1. Sequence: Months 0-6 (pre-connector): build SEO foundation ('FBA inventory + BOM software for AU brands'), recruit 1-2 design-partner FBA brands, line up 2-3 FBA podcast guest spots, partner with 1-2 FBA-specialist accounting firms (Bean Ninjas etc). Month 6-7: connector ships, launch case study, podcast tour. Months 7-9: 2-3 paid customers from design partner case studies + podcast. Months 9-12: 3-4 more via inbound + community. Year-1 contribution is supplementary not foundational — best as Phase-3 expansion leg.
profitability_math.customers_needed_for_1m_arr_aud: 214 customers at $390 ARPU. Realistic 3-year ramp: 60-120 customers if US/UK expansion pursued; 30-50 if AU-only. US/UK Amazon FBA market is the highest-volume long-term unlock but requires Phase 4+ commitment.
profitability_math.solo_founder_bandwidth_fit: 2 — Lowest of all 6 items in this batch. FBA onboarding is deep (multi-marketplace, SP-API edge cases, FNSKU/ASIN management), sales cycle is longer than expected (FBA operators are sceptical of new tools), and US/UK time-zone overlap creates support strain. Manageable at 6/year; doesn't scale to 20+/year without tooling investment or hire.
profitability_math.break_even_contribution_months: 2-3 months. $390 ARPU × 80% margin = $312/mo contribution, recovering $200-500 CAC + ~20 founder hours within 2-3 months.
profitability_math.gross_margin_sensitivity: Moderate-high. FBA support complexity (SP-API token rotation, ASIN-FNSKU mismatches, multi-marketplace currency handling) absorbs ongoing founder time. Steady-state gross margin ~75-80% (below SaaS ideal). Watch for FBA-specific support load.
profitability_math.priority_ranking: 5 — Tied with WooCommerce (item 23) as lowest priority in this batch — both Phase-3 gated. Strategic value is real (US/UK long-term unlock) but cannot drive Phase 1-2 MRR. Treat as 'Year-2 anchor' rather than near-term priority. Within Phase 3, ranks slightly behind WooCommerce due to higher onboarding complexity, lower founder credibility fit, and US-market concentration of upside (out of reach for solo founder year 1).
profitability_math.risks_and_notes: (1) Amazon SP-API integration is technically complex — requires sustained engineering investment, not just connector v1; (2) FBA inbound-shipment planning is the killer feature — basic order-sync alone is insufficient to differentiate vs SoStocked; (3) Founder credibility gap with FBA community is real — consider hiring/contracting FBA-experienced advisor or partner with named FBA voice for go-to-market; (4) Amazon itself may add native restock/inbound planning improvements that erode the wedge — watch Seller Central updates quarterly; (5) AU FBA market is too small to justify dedicated FBA connector engineering alone — only viable if US/UK expansion is on the roadmap; (6) FBA business mortality is high (account suspensions, category bans) — annual prepay + tight churn monitoring required; (7) Multi-currency / multi-marketplace pricing handling is non-trivial — scope carefully; (8) Don't promise PPC/keyword features Manuva won't ship — keep positioning to 'manufacturing + inventory + FBA inbound' lane; (9) Phase-3 decision can be deferred to month 9 review based on Phase 1-2 traction; if Phase-1 Tier A + Tier B segments deliver $3-5K MRR, consider deferring FBA connector to year 2; (10) US/UK FBA market is the real prize — AU FBA alone won't justify the build effort. Plan US expansion in parallel or defer to year 2; (11) Verify current AU Amazon-FBA seller count and revenue distribution via Marketplace Pulse before publishing TAM claims; (12) Helium 10's potential entry into BOM/manufacturing space is the biggest competitive risk — they have the audience and SaaS scale to close the wedge if they choose to.
